utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm aware that there is an urgent Prosecution motion --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There are many things that are urgent, Mr. Josse.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Your Honour, the position is this: I suspect the Trial Chamber would like to hear our submissions on that. We are quite anxious to ask for more time, and it might be the best use of the next five minutes for the Court to hear why we need more time. The Court can then decide whether to grant more time, and I could ask Mr. Butler the two minutes worth of questions tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: That's what I would suggest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You still have two minutes and not more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: That's all I need, honestly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We've got barely five minutes. There are two urgent motions. One is the latest one, to add another witness to the 65 ter list. I'm not mentioning the name in case there is a request for protective measures. It concerns mainly you, Mr. Josse. We would have preferred if you could give us your response today, but it seems that you require time.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Well, could I briefly deal with the issue of time first of all?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: As the Trial Chamber are aware, under Rule 126 bis, our response is generally within 14 days, but of course a Trial Chamber can order otherwise. This trial has proceeded smoothly and at a very sedate pace, for which we are very grateful, for the last 18 months. The Court has shown patience of all parties throughout that period. This motion is of real and fundamental importance to my client. Before responding to the motion, we want to be in a position to respond fully and accurately, and a non-exclusive list of the areas that we would like to examine before responding are: Research into the law on amending a 65 ter list so late; research into the law of this Tribunal as to what amounts to prejudice to an accused in these circumstances; research on the issue of the Office of the Prosecutor seeking to substantiate a further and significant allegation that's not on the indictment. And in addition to that, we want to be in a position to identify to you the type of investigations necessary if the motion is granted before we're in a position to cross-examine the witness. Your Honour, we are fully aware of the knock-on consequence to the schedule of this trial of what we are saying, because I should also add one other thing. In the course of our response, we will probably wish to identify those witnesses we would ask to be recalled if this witness is allowed to give her evidence. Your Honour, we are, as I've already said, fully aware of the knock-on consequence to the schedule of this trial if the application that I'm making at the moment is adhered to. But realistically, we suggest that we are entitled to a proper period of time before we respond to this motion. Clearly, the Court, with respect, isn't a bargaining shop, and I'm not seeking to enter into any negotiation with the Trial Chamber, but we would ask for a significant number of days for -- perhaps seven, before we respond to this motion. We would rather respond orally, frankly, but we'll respond in writing if we have to, but we do require more time. I repeat, we are aware of the knock-on consequences, but the situation is not of our own making. Whether it's of the Prosecution's making is something in fact we'll address in response, but it's neither here nor there. The fact is it's not of General Gvero's making nor of his lawyer's making, and we're entitled to time before we proceed to address this extremely important motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just briefly, clearly regarding the issue of 65 ter, we've -- we're all experts in those issues. There's no more research that is necessary to be done. The same thing with prejudice. This is not a genuine issue, in my view. And I can tell you this does not change the indictment or the charges in any way, shape, or form against the general, the Zepa events and the Main Staff's contribution to them. They remain the same. Having said that, yes, it's important. A few days to respond, you know, we don't have any objection to. But I also believe it's in part in the motion, this information that generated this was -- came out of I believe it was cross-examination and the constant hammering on this point over and over again by the Defence, and this is something that we're naturally following up on, and that from the moment that this came out of the witness's mouth, this has been an issue that everyone should have been ready for. So I don't see it as the big surprise that the Prosecution has created, but, yes, he should have some time to get the thoughts together and be able to respond to this. I think the weekend, and I guess we're not sitting on Monday, should be enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I would like, on my part, to address the Prosecution motion to seek to have admitted into evidence four 92 quater witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I was going to suggest, because it's time, that we deal with that. I mean, please, if you can take a joint position on that, it will be even better, and we'll deal with it tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: That's what I was going to propose, Mr. President, because it does raise some serious issues. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, definitely. Also, please think, because you mentioned the question of prejudice, try to remember the recent decision that we have taken, where I think we sent out a message that we believe that a witness is still important. We reserve the right to call that witness ourselves. So keep everything in perspective. We'll continue tomorrow -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can I send Mr. Butler -- we have another witness that has to testify and finish tomorrow, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What do you mean, send Mr. Butler?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: To his hotel to get some rest for the weekend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. No, no, what do you mean for the weekend? We are sitting tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, but we have a witness that we have -- we need to get on because he's not available to testify --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I understand Mr. Butler was flying back home on Saturday.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, I believe, is available to do what he -- to finish this up, and I certainly have some redirect to do with Mr. Butler. And given the -- this ICMP witness and the time that we see estimated by the Defence, we don't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, I also suggest you sit down together, because tomorrow we'll need to issue a revision -- an order revising the date for the conclusion of the Prosecution case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We'll start with Parsons tomorrow. You have a time limit within which you need to finish that -- the testimony of that gentleman, after which we need Mr. Butler here, and we'll continue until we finish with Mr. Butler.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 1st day of February, 2008, at 9.00 a.m. 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.50 p.m.,
